title: Zipper
content: The zippers that come with CLO3D always seem a bit underwhelming, and their size often appears too small to me. When used on the clothes, they can undermine the overall quality of the garments. That's why I've specifically crafted #5 - sized zippers. There are two types, and each type has two closure methods. All the attributes and adjustment methods of these zippers are fully compatible with the software. I typically apply them to the making of down jackets and padded jackets, which endows the clothing with an overall sense of luxury. I've set up UV grid layouts for both the zippers and their pulls, enabling the customization of LOGOs, just as shown in my illustrations. The UV grids are directly incorporated into the normal map of each zipper file, and the file format is.PSD. After downloading, you can click to make modifications. I'm still in the process of continuous exploration, hoping to offer more convenient methods to enthusiasts!![2430ead84cb140e68e6af7a5a9630abd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/15c014faef94469c93dde357b5fc4cb2/images/2430ead84cb140e68e6af7a5a9630abd%E7%AC%AC%E4%BA%8C%E7%89%88.png)
content_description: Discover custom #5-sized zippers designed for CLO3D that enhance garment quality, featuring adjustable attributes, UV grid layouts for logo customization, and full compatibility with your designs.

title: Creating a non-human avatar with odd shape in MD
content:
I'm using Marvelous Designer, and I have a character that was designed elsewhere, but I need to create new clothing for it. The character is pretty much a ball of fur with legs - think Mike Wazowski from Monsters, Inc but with no arms. I've tried creating a placeholder (unrigged) obj file in Cinema and importing it, but being the shape it is, setting the body points in the Avatar Editor and creating a fitting suit isn't really working (the suit keeps tearing). And for the life of me I can't figure out how to create custom arrangement points. I do not need it to be animated/in motion, but I do need it to be realistic and properly draped. The plan is to bring the created clothing back into Cinema4D for final render with my character. 

I've had difficulty finding any information about creating your own avatar, and even less about non-human avatars. I would appreciate if anyone has any tips/tricks they could share, or any tutorials they could point me towards. Thanks in advance!


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Don’t use Fitting Suit at all. Instead, draft simple patterns manually and arrange them using Arrangement Points or Bounding Volumes (spheres work better for round characters).In the Avatar Editor, avoid setting standard body points. For non-humans, MD doesn’t rely on them correctly and this often causes tearing.Increase particle distance first (20–30), simulate, then gradually lower it after the garment settles.If arrangement points are limited, create temporary helper geometry (simple spheres/cylinders) as separate avatars to guide placement, then delete them later.
Reply 1: Thank you. I still have questions based on your reply, but I'm going to try some stuff out based on this before I ask.
content_description: This webpage serves as a resource for tips and tutorials on creating custom clothing for non-human avatars in Marvelous Designer, specifically for those facing challenges with unique character shapes and arrangement points.
